analyst_view.overall: Sporting (10th, 9 points) host Manchester United (17th, 6 points); a win would put Sporting close to the top-eight places, while United need points to stay in the play-off spots. Both clubs have new coaches: Paulo Fonseca replaced Rui Borges at Sporting in early November, and United sacked Michael Carrick on 12 November with the team in the Premier League relegation zone and appointed Mauricio Pochettino, whose first game is at Liverpool on Sunday, so this is only his second. United are without Matheus Cunha (one-match ban for his red card against Roma, which the numbers already count) and striker Sesko, out since October with a shin problem, plus Shaw, Rashford, Baleba and Ugarte according to one availability list; Sesko's absence is already part of United's recent form. Sporting's Zalazar is back from a thigh injury with a minor knee complaint. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already take Cunha's suspension off United (about -9% on their goals). United have leaked goals lately (16 conceded in 6), and a new coach could tighten them up or still be finding his feet in his second game, so the change points neither way. Sesko has been out for weeks, so his absence is already in their form; I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, with United slightly more of them. Fonseca's Sporting like to build through the middle and Pochettino's teams press high, but neither coach has had time to change much, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already lowered for Sporting's quiet recent record and raised for United's busy one (16 cards in 6). Cunha, who was sent off for two yellows against Roma, is suspended, which removes one hot-headed player, but that is small, and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, with United's recent shot volume adding about 10% to their side. Without Cunha and Sesko, United's attack leans on Mbeumo, Fernandes and Amad, which the numbers partly reflect; nothing new points either way, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, split evenly. Sporting at home under Fonseca and a United side in coaching transition make it hard to call a direction, and the key absences are already counted or already in recent form, so I stay at 10.2.
